grounds: The finding rests on a wrong premise about which file holds a session specification. The sessions root has ONE hand-written plan, docs/sessions/session-plan.md: it is SESSION_PLAN_FILENAME in ai_router/evidence.py, the file build_projection reads its "### Session N:" headings from (ai_router/progress.py), and PLAN_FILENAME in the extension scan (fileSystem.ts), which is where the prompt now derives the path from via repository.planPath rather than a typed filename. docs/sessions/project-work-plan.md is NOT a specification: it is one of the two prose files writers.py folds out of activity-log.json on every append, and the build instructions say never to hand-edit it because an edit survives exactly until the next append. Directing the rewrite there, as the finding proposes, would send the engine into a machine-owned file the framework forbids editing. The second half, that the selected block must be rewritten in place and re-registered, is impossible under the lifecycle the record enforces: session.start refuses a closed number ("Sessions are never re-opened"), and a rounds ledger is append-only per number with the cap counted over it, so a rewritten specification can only run as a NEW number with a fresh ledger. The prompt says this and hands the engine the three commands that exist for it: cancel --force for an unresolved session, the new "### Session M:" entry in the plan, and session start. That is the rewrite-and-reregister sequence the lifecycle admits; the one the finding asks for does not exist.
